security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU writes the full (unshifted) physical address or guest physical address to pdisadr2 sample record field for explicit memory access samples, instead of shifting the address right by 2 bits as required by the spec change. Conversely, QEMU applies the right-shift-by-2 encoding but guest software (or another QEMU component) interprets pdisadr2 as a full unshifted address, causing a 4x mismatch in physical address values.
security_spec.summary: Physical/guest-physical addresses written to pdisadr2 must be right-shifted by 2 bits matching PMP-address encoding; failure to apply or consume this shift corrupts guest physical address data in PDIS sample records, leaking wrong addresses to the guest profiler.

findings.finding: The Sspdis (pointer discovery) extension is not implemented in QEMU. No CSR registration, read/write handlers, or mask definitions exist for pdisadr2, spdisdata, or any pointer-discovery sample-record fields. The entire feature—including the physical address right-shift-by-2 encoding for pdisadr2—is absent from the codebase.
findings.snippet:
uint64_t mask = MENVCFG_FIOM | MENVCFG_CBIE | MENVCFG_CBCFE |
                    MENVCFG_CBZE | MENVCFG_CDE;

findings.finding: RV32 menvcfgh high-half write path likewise has no pointer-discovery support. No spdisdata or related CSR fields are handled in any menvcfg write path.
findings.snippet:
uint64_t mask = (cfg->ext_svpbmt ? MENVCFG_PBMTE : 0) |
                    (cfg->ext_sstc ? MENVCFG_STCE : 0) |
                    (cfg->ext_svadu ? MENVCFG_ADUE : 0) |
                    (cfg->ext_smcdeleg ? MENVCFG_CDE : 0) |
                    (cfg->ext_ssdbltrp ? MENVCFG_DTE : 0);

findings.finding: The IOMMU device-context validation code is unrelated to pointer discovery. The newly added check validates that MSIPTP mode is OFF when GATP mode is BARE—a purely IOMMU-level architectural constraint with no connection to sample-record address fields.
